decision: Run-3 Owner Decision 1 — the opportunity post's `decide-by` date
ratified_option: B — derived by default, always present, overridable

ids_allocated.summary: Every post has a decide-by; derived from D-10's type-scoped date semantics, overridable, a real asked field on brief/RFP and open call, a terms field under D-09, and the date that closes the post.
The decide-by is a real, asked field on this type, and it is the same date D-04 already publishes as the expected decision date.
Does D-06's `time-to-close` clock read the post's date or its decide-by?

tracked_questions_left_open.question: Does D-06's `time-to-close` clock read the post's date (submission close) or its decide-by (post close)?
tracked_questions_left_open.why_not_answered_here: The canonical statement defines the dates and says nothing about alert tiering, so the answer is not licensed by this ratification. The escalation spends alert 2 of 2 (04.02.04 D-12), so guessing is expensive: a wrong reading either burns a recipient's last alert months early or never fires it.
tracked_questions_left_open.divergence_scope: Only brief/RFP and open call (04.07) — the two types carrying an asked decide-by. On the ten derived types both dates are the same instant and D-06 is unchanged.
tracked_questions_left_open.proposed_but_unratified: time-to-close = time to submission close (the earlier of the post's date and its decide-by), since the alert exists to prompt an application; the decide-by is what the applicant is later told under 04.04.01 D-06.

terms_field_call.verdict: YES — the decide-by is a D-09 terms field.
terms_field_call.reasoning: A poster who silently pushes 'you'll hear by 14 Aug' out to 30 Sep has ghosted every waiting applicant while the UI keeps showing them a date — precisely the harm the 04.05 sub-domain exists to price. D-09's own governing principle is that no field invents its own handling, so an operational-field carve-out would be the divergent semantics D-09 was written to prevent.
terms_field_call.consequences: Editing the decide-by on a live post with >=1 submission re-gates, notifies every submitter with the specific delta, and offers a one-tap withdraw, with D-09's uniform silence default (no response = applicant STAYS). Shortening notifies on the same rule.
terms_field_call.no_double_notify_rule: Where the decide-by is derived, a change to its base date carries it and both appear in the SAME delta — one notification, never two. Recorded in D-09's row and as an edge-case row.

expiry_contradiction_reconciliation.was: 04.01.01:176 closed the post when the EVENT date passed, while 04.05.01:68, 04.05.01:147 and 04.04.01:136 all asserted an auto-close at the DECIDE-BY.
expiry_contradiction_reconciliation.now: Two distinct events, both stated in the state tables. The post's date closes SUBMISSION; the decide-by closes the POST (every open slot -> `closed`, close-out obligation fires per 04.05.01).
expiry_contradiction_reconciliation.why_it_is_not_a_behaviour_change_for_mos: On the ten derived types the decide-by IS the post's date, so both events land on the same instant and the old one-date rule is the special case of the new one.
expiry_contradiction_reconciliation.where_they_diverge: Brief/RFP and open call (04.07), which carry an asked decide-by, and any post whose poster lengthened the derived value.
expiry_contradiction_reconciliation.shortening_case: A poster who shortens the decide-by below the post's date closes both at the earlier of the two — a poster who has stopped deciding must stop collecting applications.
expiry_contradiction_reconciliation.new_state_added: `Submission closed`, at slot level and post level, for the window between the two dates.
